name: Texas State University Police Department
whatItDoes: 24/7 response on campus. Emergency call boxes across campus connect directly to UPD and share your location. Can take a criminal report.
doesNotRequire: Nothing. Available to anyone, any hour.
location: Pecan Building, 1321 Academy St, San Marcos

name: HCWC HELPline (Hays-Caldwell Women's Center)
whatItDoes: 24/7 confidential crisis line. Safety planning, danger assessment, emergency shelter, help filing protective orders, attorney referral, court accompaniment. Free.
doesNotRequire: No police report. No university involvement. Confidential, and not a mandatory reporter.
location: San Marcos, serving Hays and Caldwell counties

name: Hays County Crisis Hotline
whatItDoes: Countywide crisis line covering domestic violence, sexual assault, and mental health crisis.

name: Protective Order (Hays County)
whatItDoes: A civil court order restricting contact and proximity. Separate track from any criminal case. HCWC provides free legal advocacy and attorney referral to file one.
doesNotRequire: You do not need a criminal case, a conviction, or a police report to apply.

name: Office of Equal Opportunity and Title IX
whatItDoes: University process for sexual misconduct, dating violence, and stalking. Supportive measures include no contact directives, housing relocation, and academic accommodations. Reports can be filed for someone else, anonymously, or under a pseudonym.
doesNotRequire: No police report needed. Supportive measures can be requested without a full investigation.
location: Elliott Hall A, 3rd Floor, 201 Talbot St
note: Under Texas SB 212, most university employees are mandatory reporters. Telling a supervisor or faculty member typically triggers a report to Title IX.

name: Report It (Texas State)
whatItDoes: Central reporting portal that routes to the correct office, including the Title IX reporting form.

name: CARE Center, Dean of Students
whatItDoes: Helps students impacted by an emergency or crisis. Coordinates across university offices and the San Marcos community for practical support.

name: Dean of Students Office
whatItDoes: Interim measures, absence notifications, and general advocacy when something disrupts your ability to attend or function.

name: Attorney for Students
whatItDoes: Free legal counsel for enrolled students, limited scope representation, and guidance on your legal rights and options.

name: Texas State Counseling Center
whatItDoes: Free confidential brief counseling and crisis response for enrolled students. TimelyCare offers virtual on demand emotional support outside office hours.
note: Outside business hours, select option 2 for crisis support.

name: Student Health Center
whatItDoes: On campus medical care. Registered nurse reachable after hours, including nights, weekends, and holidays.

name: HCWC Counseling and Resource Center
whatItDoes: Free short term counseling, up to six months, for survivors of family violence, dating violence, and sexual assault in Hays and Caldwell counties.

name: National Domestic Violence Hotline
whatItDoes: 24/7 support and referral to the nearest local program, anywhere in the country.

name: RAINN National Sexual Assault Hotline
whatItDoes: 24/7 confidential support, routed to a trained staff member at a local affiliate. Online chat also available.

name: 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline
whatItDoes: 24/7 mental health crisis support by call, text, or chat.
